title: Overcoming sluggish austenite reversion in medium-Mn steels by suppressing carbide precipitation
abstract: Austenite reversion in cold-rolled medium-Mn steels is sluggish due to carbide precipitation, and prolonged annealing is often required to obtain sufficient austenite and regain tensile ductility. Here, we overcome this kinetic bottleneck by introducing pre-existing austenite into the initial microstructure. The pre-existing austenite efficiently absorbs carbon and manganese from the supersaturated martensitic matrix, reaching concentrations that exceed thermodynamic equilibrium values. This solute uptake rapidly depletes carbon in the matrix, thereby suppressing carbide precipitation that would otherwise retard austenite formation. Consequently, the accelerated reversion delivers an outstanding synergy of 1.1 GPa yield strength and 22% uniform elongation after 2-min annealing, whereas 120-min annealing is required to achieve comparable ductility in steels without pre-existing austenite. These findings demonstrate carbide suppression via pre-existing austenite as an effective strategy to accelerate reversion and develop high-performance steels compatible with industrial continuous annealing lines.
